topics.title: Global water resources: Distribution and historical impact

cards.definition: A glacier is a large, slow-moving mass of ice formed from layers of compacted snow.
An aquifer is a layer of rock or soil deep underground that holds water. This water can be taken out using wells and pumps.
A civilisation is a large, organised group of people with cities, laws, farming, trade, and inventions like Ancient Egypt or the Indus Valley.

image.alt: A world map marking where early civilisations and early farming began along river valleys.
image.caption: Ancient river valley civilisations

cards.definition: Irrigation is a way of bringing water to crops using pipes, canals, or sprinklers to help plants grow, especially in dry places.

image.alt: A farm field of green crop rows being watered by sprinklers.
image.caption: Smart irrigation

cards.definition: Migration is the movement of people, animals, or birds from one place to another, often for food, shelter, breeding, or better living conditions.
Sanitation means keeping our surroundings clean and healthy by properly removing waste, dirty water and preventing the spread of germs.
Contaminated means polluted or made unsafe by harmful substances, germs, or waste.

image.alt: People standing in a river covered with white toxic foam.
image.caption: Chhat Puja in a polluted, toxic Yamuna river

topics.title: Water's properties and its role in daily life

cards.definition: Condensation is when warm water vapour in the air cools down and changes back into water droplets like clouds in the sky or water on a cold glass.

image.alt: Thick white mist hanging over a dark green pine forest.
image.caption: Water vapour appears as mist in the forest

cards.definition: Sublimation is when ice or snow changes directly into water vapour can happen on mountain tops.

image.alt: A diagram of water as gas, liquid and solid with arrows labelled vaporization, condensation, sublimation, deposition, freezing and melting.
image.caption: States of water

cards.definition: Surface tension is a special force on the top of water that holds the water together this is why small insects can walk on water!

image.alt: A water strider insect standing on the surface of a pond.
image.caption: Water strider, using surface tension to walk

cards.definition: Cohesion means water sticks to itself (like water droplets joining together), and adhesion means water sticks to other things (like water climbing up a plant stem).
Capillary action is the movement of liquid through narrow spaces or tiny tubes without being pushed by an outside force.
Density is the amount of matter packed into a given space or volume.
Latent heat is the hidden heat water carries when it changes form for example, when water evaporates or when vapour turns back into water as rain.

topics.title: Water and climate: Change, impact, and action

cards.definition: Climate change means big changes in weather patterns over a long time, often caused by pollution and too many greenhouse gases.

image.alt: Two satellite views of the Arctic, September 1984 and September 2016, the later one with much less white sea ice.
image.caption: Shrinking Arctic ice-cap

cards.definition: Wetlands are areas of land where water covers the soil or keeps it wet for most or all of the year, supporting special plants and animals.
Desalination is the process of removing salt from seawater so it can be used for drinking and farming.
Drip irrigation is a method of supplying water slowly and directly to the roots of plants through small pipes or tubes.

topics.title: Life in water – Aquatic ecosystems and biodiversity

cards.definition: Biodiversity means having many different types of plants and animals living together in a habitat.

image.alt: A collage of four freshwater animals: an alligator, a trout, an otter and a frog.
image.caption: Freshwater aquatic animals

cards.definition: Salinity is the amount of dissolved salts present in water or soil.
Phytoplankton are tiny plant-like organisms that live in water and make their own food using sunlight.

image.alt: A colourful drawing of many tiny floating plankton of different shapes in blue-green water.
image.caption: Phytoplanktons

cards.definition: A decomposer is a tiny organism like a fungus or bacteria that breaks down dead things and returns nutrients to the soil or water.
A food web shows how plants and animals are connected by what they eat like a big map of who eats whom in an ecosystem.

image.alt: An ocean food chain diagram from sunlight to phytoplankton, zooplankton, small fishes, tuna and a shark, with arrows showing the direction of energy.
image.caption: Movement of energy through different levels of food chain

cards.definition: Buoyant means able to float or rise in a liquid or gas because of an upward force.
Adaptation is a special body part or behaviour that helps an animal or plant survive in its home like gills in fish or webbed feet in ducks.

image.alt: The head of a fish with its gill cover open, showing the red feathery gills inside.
image.caption: Gills filter oxygen from sea water

cards.definition: An ecosystem is a place where living things like animals and plants work together with non-living things like water, air, and soil.
